title: [Workshop] AI Engineering 201: Inference
talk_summary: A broad 2023-era workshop on inference fundamentals: build-vs-buy for models, where inference runs (device/browser/cloud/self-hosted), why GPUs are used (memory-bandwidth vs FLOPs), batching, and profiling.

takeaways.what_they_do: Explains that throughput comes from batching many inputs, but latency-sensitive serving must balance FLOP-bound and memory-bound regimes, and KV-cache is only worth it when not already memory-bound.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you're doing something that's an API where like serving requests directly then you would want to like roughly balance being uh flop bound and memory bound
takeaways.numbers: A100 flips from memory-bound to compute-bound around batch size ~200

takeaways.what_they_do: Argues you should use a profiler/tracer rather than reason from first principles, citing a real bug where per-element CUDA kernel launches cost throughput.
takeaways.evidence_quote: even like people who are pretty good at this will like Miss stuff that shows up on a on a tracer
takeaways.numbers: Fixing per-element kernel launches gave ~33% throughput increase

takeaways.technique: Cold-start cost of loading large artifacts
takeaways.what_they_do: Notes serverless GPU cold boots are dominated by moving huge weights into accelerator memory, showing up as p99 latency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're looking at like 30C 1 minute 3 minute cold boots in some cases cuz you are moving a half a terabyte of data

takeaways.technique: Capability saturation argument for cheaper models
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues open/cheaper models catch up once capability requirements saturate, so pick the cheapest model that is 'smart enough' rather than always the top model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if capabilities requirements saturate if people no longer want the absolute smartest model out there they just want a model smart enough for XYZ then open models will probably catch up

takeaways.what_they_do: Shows that style-finetuned models win human 'looks good' votes while being factually wrong, warning against preference-based evaluation without grounding.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it didn't have any grounding in the actual utility of the answers it was just a lot of people going like looks good to me
